content.rendered:
When Southside Johnny released his first solo album in 1988, he called upon his old friend Bruce Springsteen to help him close out the record. The album’s final song is a moody ballad called “Walking Through Midnight” co-written by Southside and Bruce.

Southside penned the lyrics, and Bruce composed the music. Neither of them brought their A game to it, though: the late-night wandering lyrics aren’t particularly inspired, and the backing track is about as late-eighties pop as it gets.

Still, any Lyon/Springsteen collaboration is worth at least one listen, even one as under the radar as “Walking Through Midnight.”

(And we’re talking seriously under the radar here: If either of them have ever performed the song live, I’m not aware of it.)

Walking Through Midnight
Released: Slow Dance (1988)
Never performed 

© June 15, 2020

excerpt.rendered: One of the more under-the-radar Southside Johnny/Bruce Springsteen collaborations, “Walking Through Midnight” closed Southside’s first solo album in 1988.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Keep A-Knockin’
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce took a few runs at Little Richard's "Keep A-Knockin'." Listen to two of them here: one with Midnight Thunder, the other with Southside Johnny and The Asbury Jukes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chain of Fools
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins Southside Johnny and Graham Parker to cover one of Aretha Franklin's greatest hits.

jetpack-related-posts.title: It Ain’t the Meat (It’s the Motion)
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce and the E Street Band join the Asbury Jukes (minus Southside Johnny) to cover one of rock's earlier risque classics.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Trapped Again
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce co-wrote "Trapped Again" with Southside Johnny and Steve Van Zandt, but he's only performed it live once. Check it out inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Down in the Valley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce covers Solomon Burke's country soul classic with Southside Johnny and The Asbury Jukes in 1977.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Funky Broadway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins short-lived Stone Pony house band The Shots for a cover of Wilson Pickett's hit, "Funky Broadway."
